title: Liouvillian Non-Invertible Symmetry
authors: Ying-Cheng Yang, Jhen-Dong Lin, Yueh-Nan Chen
abstract: Non-invertible symmetries extend conventional symmetries beyond group-like transformations and play an important role in quantum field theory and many-body physics. However, a general framework of non-invertible symmetries in open quantum systems is still lacking. Here, we formulate a general Liouville-space duality framework that extends Hilbert-space non-invertible dualities to open quantum systems. The resulting defect relates Liouvillians with dual Hamiltonian and dissipative parameters and becomes an exact symmetry at self-duality. We apply this framework to the periodic transverse-field Ising chain with two collective Lindblad channels exchanged by Kramers--Wannier (KW) duality. A strong $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry divides Liouville space into four parity sectors, while the defect acts nontrivially only in the even-even sector. At self-duality, the KW defect imposes a momentum-resolved selection rule on Liouvillian Jordan blocks. Modes with different Liouville momenta or KW-defect eigenvalues cannot form a common exceptional Jordan block. For a three-site chain, a global Rényi-2 KW asymmetry dynamically identifies the self-dual conditions. At the same time, the spectral structure exhibits both a semisimple degeneracy and a self-dual exceptional point with a perturbation-selective response. These results extend non-invertible dualities to Markovian quantum dynamics and establish a symmetry-based selection rule for Liouvillian Jordan structures.
summary: This paper extends the concept of non-invertible symmetries to open quantum systems by formulating a Liouville-space duality framework. Applying this to the Ising chain, the authors show that the symmetry imposes strict selection rules on the Liouvillian's spectral structure. This allows for the precise identification and characterization of self-dual exceptional points in the dynamics.
main_problem: The paper develops a general framework for non-invertible symmetries in open quantum systems, extending known dualities from Hilbert space to the Liouville space formalism.
main_result: It establishes a Liouville-space duality relation for the open system dynamics and derives a momentum-resolved selection rule for Liouvillian Jordan blocks, distinguishing between semisimple degeneracies and self-dual exceptional points.
method: The authors utilize a Liouville-space duality framework, applying Kramers-Wannier (KW) duality to the periodic transverse-field Ising chain to analyze the constraints imposed by non-invertible symmetries on the spectral structure.
model_or_system: The model is the periodic transverse-field Ising chain undergoing Markovian dynamics governed by a Lindblad master equation. The analysis focuses on the Liouvillian superoperator and its symmetries.
key_observables: Liouvillian spectrum, exceptional points (EPs), the global Rényi-2 KW asymmetry ($\Delta S^{(2)}_{KW,glob}$), and the structure of Jordan blocks.
important_parameters: The system parameters include coupling constants ($J, g$) and dissipation rates ($\gamma_A, \gamma_B$). Self-duality is achieved when $J=g$ and $\gamma_A = \gamma_B$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to Markovian dynamics governed by the Lindblad equation, and the framework relies on the existence of a general Liouville-space duality.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Liouville-space extension of KW symmetry, the vanishing of the global second-Rényi KW asymmetry at self-dual points, and the mapping of exceptional degeneracies in parameter space.
paper_structure: The paper first formulates the Liouville-space duality, then applies it to the TFIM using KW duality, analyzing the resulting symmetry constraints on the Liouvillian Jordan structure, culminating in a detailed spectral analysis of the reduced dynamics at the self-dual point.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, symmetry-based tool to analyze non-Hermitian quantum dynamics (open systems), which is crucial for understanding dissipation and non-equilibrium steady states in condensed matter and quantum optics.

Generic points on these curves are EP2s. The red circles mark EP3s, and the black cross marks a semisimple degeneracy. The green dashed line denotes the self-dual condition γA = γB, whose unique intersection with the EP2 locus in L++ is marked by the yellow star at (γA, γB) = (2/3, 2/3). The yellow diamond marks an isolated EP2 shared by L+−and L−+, while the yellow circle marks an isolated EP2 in L−−.
